title: How Much Is an Eighth of Weed? 3.5 Grams Explained

body:
How much is an eighth? An eighth is one-eighth of an ounce of cannabis, sold as 3.5 grams. It's small enough to try something new and big enough for several sessions, which is why it turns up on so many flower menus. Here's what an eighth of weed in grams really means, what it looks like, how many joints it rolls, what moves its price and how it fits within Michigan's limits.

## How much is an eighth? 3.5 grams

Cannabis is weighed in grams but sold in old fractions of an ounce. An ounce is about 28.35 grams, menus round it to 28, and one-eighth of that is 3.5. The exact eighth is about 3.54 grams, a gap of a few hundredths of a gram. So when a menu lists 3.5 grams of weed, it's an eighth.

## What an eighth looks like

Picture a few medium buds, or one large bud and some smaller ones, sitting loosely in a small jar. Bud density changes the picture a lot: a tight, heavy eighth can look much smaller than a fluffy one. Licensed packages list their net weight, so the label settles any doubt.

## Slang for an eighth

- **An eighth** or **an 8th**
- **A three-and-a-half** or **a 3.5**, for the grams
- **An eighth-ounce**, the long form

## How many joints in an eighth?

It depends on how much flower goes into each joint.

| Joint size | Flower per joint | Joints from an eighth |
|---|---|---|
| Slim | 0.3 g | About 11 |
| Standard | 0.5 g | 7 |
| Large | 1 g | 3, with a little left over |

Researchers who analyzed more than 10,000 U.S. cannabis purchases estimated the average joint at about 0.31 to 0.32 grams. At that size, an eighth rolls about 11.

## Eighth vs. gram: value per gram

An eighth usually costs more per gram than a [quarter](/blog/how-much-is-a-quarter-of-marijuana/) or a [half](/blog/how-much-is-a-half-of-marijuana/), but less than buying single grams. To compare, divide the eighth's price by 3.5 and set it next to a gram's price. Bigger isn't automatically better: an eighth you enjoy beats a half you don't. Our [cannabis measurements chart](/blog/how-many-grams-ounce-marijuana/) shows every size side by side.

## What moves the price

The eighth price you see depends on several things:

- **Quality tier.** Premium, carefully trimmed buds cost more than smalls or shake.
- **Potency and strain.** High-THC flower and in-demand strains usually cost more.
- **Taxes.** Adult-use purchases carry a 10% excise tax plus the 6% sales tax, which is figured on the price including the excise, for about 16.6% in total. Registered medical patients pay only the 6% sales tax.
- **Wholesale tax.** As of October 2026, a 24% wholesale tax has applied since January 1, 2026, when growers and processors first sell adult-use cannabis to retailers. It doesn't appear on your receipt, but it can be passed along.
- **Deals and rewards.** Promotions change, and our free loyalty program, [The Society](/club-member-program/), adds points to qualifying purchases.

Current prices are on your store's [menu](/shop/).

## Why the eighth became a standard jar size

The eighth is the smallest of the common ounce fractions, so it's a low-commitment way to buy a strain by weight. That makes it practical in a few ways:

- **Easy to try.** You can sample a strain's aroma and flavor without stocking up.
- **Easy to finish fresh.** A small amount gets used before it dries out.
- **Easy to compare.** Two different eighths let you judge, side by side, how each one smells and feels to you.

## What an eighth is good for

An eighth covers a lot of ground for an occasional consumer: a handful of joints, several bowls or a few weekends of sessions. It's also the natural way to explore. If you're learning what you like, our guide to [cannabis flower](/blog/cannabis-flower-101/) explains how to read strain types, potency and aroma, and an eighth gives you a low-stakes way to put that into practice.

## Michigan possession limits

Michigan's limits leave plenty of room for an eighth:

- **Carrying.** Adults 21 and older may carry up to 2.5 ounces, which is 20 eighths, with a 15-gram cap on concentrate.
- **Buying.** Licensed adult-use stores can sell up to 2.5 ounces per transaction and check government-issued photo ID before every sale.
- **At home.** The home limit is 10 ounces plus your own plants' harvest, and anything over 2.5 ounces has to be kept locked.
- **In the car.** Using cannabis while driving is off-limits, and so is smoking in a vehicle's passenger area on a public road. Keeping your purchase sealed and out of reach, such as in the trunk, is the cautious habit.
- **Across borders.** Don't travel across state lines with cannabis.

For the full rundown, see our guide to [Michigan cannabis laws](/cannabis-laws-by-state/michigan/). 21+ only. Please consume responsibly.

faq.q: How many grams is an eighth?
faq.a: Three and a half on a dispensary menu. An ounce is about 28.35 grams; menus round it to 28, and an eighth of that is 3.5 grams. The exact figure is about 3.54 grams, a small gap you'd only notice on a precise home scale.

faq.q: How many joints does an eighth make?
faq.a: Roughly 3 to 11, depending on size. A full-gram joint uses almost a third of an eighth, so you'd get three. At half a gram you'd get seven, and at 0.3 grams about eleven. Research on more than 10,000 U.S. purchases put the average joint at about a third of a gram.

Because it's a practical size. It's the smallest common fraction of an ounce, so it costs less up front than a quarter or a half, and it's enough for several sessions. That makes it an easy way to try a new strain and decide whether you like it before buying more.

faq.q: How long does an eighth last?
faq.a: It depends on how you use it. If you roll half-gram joints and enjoy one a week, an eighth lasts about seven weeks. Someone who uses a little every day might finish it within a week. Keep it in an airtight jar away from heat and light so it stays fresh.

review.notes: The brief H1 called the eighth "the most popular size"; no source was opened for that, so the copy says it is a familiar, standard jar size and explains why, without ranking it. The homepage buy-two-get-one eighth deal is not cited (time-bound). No prices. Fact-check 2026-10-24: 16 claims checked; NIST, Ridgeway & Kilmer (full text) and Smart 2017 opened; figures recomputed; Michigan law and taxes against law-facts; rewards against hs-facts. Fixed: an unsupported 'half the size' figure and the overstated 'smallest/lowest-commitment' line; linked The Society to its program page. Cross-batch sweep 2026-10-24 (orchestrator, after the fact-check workflow): hs-facts records every captured deal on all 8 store pages, so the article no longer says deals differ by store (the /deals/ page keeps its own hedge, docs/OPEN-DECISIONS.md item 8).
